messages:
Ethan: FYI CI started failing for flash_paged wheel after the builder image bump to bookworm.
Mira: what failure are you seeing?
Ethan: ImportError on import: undefined symbol memcpy@GLIBC_2.32 when loading libflash.so from the wheel.
Jordan: sounds like glibc symbol versioning mismatch — which base image changed?
Ethan: bookworm instead of bullseye; glibc now 2.34. The packager image got swapped in the release job.
Priya: curious: do we build wheels with manylinux? If yes, symbol versions should be constrained.
Ethan: we do, but the test harness that installs the wheel runs inside a container with newer glibc and some prebuilt object in the wheel picks up newer symbol requirements.
Sam: can you paste readelf -V output?
Ethan: sure:
```
readelf -V dist/flash_paged/libflash.so | grep memcpy
  memcpy@@GLIBC_2.32
```
Tony: that triples with a kernel selection problem we saw: some nodes fall back to naive paged kernel causing perf regressions.
Mira: we observed a ~12% p99 increase for long sequences on staging after the packaging change and some runs log `kernel_select: reason=missing_isa chosen=naive_paged`.
Jordan: missing_isa implies the kernel artifact was compiled without AVX2/AVX512 flags. Did LTO or build flags change in the image?
Ethan: Bookworm's toolchain uses GCC12 defaults and our Dockerfile lost explicit -march flags in one layer. Also LTO combined some objects made elsewhere.
Priya: plausible root cause for both symbol version and missing ISA. Action plan?
Sam: bisect: 1) rerun packaging with pinned bullseye builder, 2) rebuild libflash with explicit -march=skylake-avx512 and test selection.
Mira: also add CI checks: run readelf -V on built shared libs and assert no newer GLIBC symbol versions; fail otherwise.
Tony: I'll open a MR for a packaging guard script and add objdump/grep checks.
Sam: adding a CI job now: tools/ci/check-glibc-symbols.sh and a matrix entry.
Jordan: runtime change: have kernel_select emit detailed reason codes (missing_isa, incompatible_symbol) and attach metrics so we can correlate KV hit rate drops.
Ethan: repro done locally: building under bookworm gave short-seq throughput -9%, long-seq p99 +16%, KV hit-rate from 0.92->0.79.
Mira: ugly but actionable. Short-term: pin manylinux2014/bullseye for packaging to stabilize wheels. Long-term: unify compile flags across toolchain, and avoid embedding prebuilt objects from the base image.
Priya: schedule: Ethan to repro+rebuild on pinned image and post perf counters (EOD). Sam to collect perf counters for both builds. Jordan to land kernel_select logs. Mira to pin packaging image MR.
ci-bot: JOB 5021 flash_paged-wheel-packaging FAILED — https://ci.internal/5021
Ethan: I'll attach perf flamegraphs in the MR.
Mira: thanks everyone — sync tomorrow after the perf numbers. :thumbsup:
